subject: Medforge Community Makerspace Development
overview: Host John Petrella interviewed Trey Winter regarding the growth of the Medforge Community Makerspace, a non-profit initiative providing residents with access to industrial tools and craft education. The discussion detailed the organization's search for a permanent facility, its educational workshops, and upcoming community fundraising efforts.

items.title: Guest background and local history
items.summary: Host John Petrella introduced Trey Winter, who discussed his transition from professional work at the Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory to becoming an active member of the Medford community.

items.title: Medforge origins and mission
items.summary: Winter explained how the loss of local makerspace access during the pandemic inspired him to research and launch a community-driven organization for artists and tradespeople.

items.title: Facility search and city partnerships
items.summary: The organization is collaborating with the city and Ware Street Workplaces to secure a 10,000-square-foot warehouse on Riverside Avenue, supported by a pending $1.3 million grant application.

items.title: Community and economic significance
items.summary: The discussion highlighted how makerspaces support trade skills like welding and provide local venues for arts and entertainment to keep resident spending within the city.

items.title: Institutional collaborations and library passes
items.summary: Medforge established a partnership with the Medford Library to offer day passes for patrons and currently operates programming out of the Arts Collaborative Medford facility.

items.title: Household tool educational series
items.summary: A city grant funded the 'Intro to Household Tools' series, which provides hands-on training for basic home maintenance tasks like shelf installation and drywall repair.

items.title: Welcome to Deadford Halloween fundraiser
items.summary: Medforge will host its 'Welcome to Deadford' fundraiser on October 31, featuring custom 3D-printed gothic decor and local sponsorships.

items.title: Future programming and open studios
items.summary: Winter announced upcoming participation in the Medford Open Studios on November 14 and plans for inter-city makerspace mentoring.

items.title: Membership and accessibility model
items.summary: The organization plans to offer tiered membership options, including volunteer-based access to remove financial barriers for residents.
